metadata.summary: MedMNIST is a collection of standardized, pre-processed medical image classification datasets covering 18 (v1) / 20+ (v2) tasks across diverse modalities (dermoscopy, X-ray, OCT, pathology, chest CT, retinal, etc.), at small uniform resolutions (28x28 / 64x64 / 128x128 for 2D, 28x28x28 for 3D). It aggregates ~708K 2D images and ~10K 3D images from existing public sources, intended as an educational benchmark for reproducible ML rather than a clinical-scale resource.
metadata.purpose: Educational benchmark for reproducible machine learning research in medical imaging.
metadata.avoided_uses: Real-world clinical deployment; tasks requiring high-resolution diagnostic detail.

papers.title: MedMNIST v2: A Large-Scale Lightweight Benchmark for 2D/3D Medical Image Classification

modality.scope: Multi-organ, multi-disease classification tasks (e.g., skin lesion, chest pathology, retinal disease, breast mass).

ethics.privacy_measures: Data are de-identified and pre-processed; original source datasets underwent de-identification prior to inclusion.
ethics.legal_compliance: Compliance depends on upstream source licenses; users must verify terms for each sub-dataset.

extraction.notes: Baseline card derived solely from dataset_catalog.xlsx real metadata; remaining fields require paper/README or manual completion.
pending_verification: The following LLM fields were auto-dropped for violating schema constraints and reverted to baseline; pending manual review: data_collection_setting, modality/modalities[list-items]

known_limitations: Tiny image resolution (e.g., 28x28) limits clinical relevance and feature fidelity.
Designed for education/reproducibility, not real-world deployment.
Class balance and label quality inherited from heterogeneous upstream sources.
No standardized demographic reporting across sub-datasets.
bias_and_limitations.modifications: Pre-processed and resampled to uniform low resolutions; labels unchanged.
bias_and_limitations.representativeness_concerns: Not designed for population representativeness; reflects availability and licensing of public sources.
bias_and_limitations.long_tail_classes: Varies by sub-dataset; some exhibit long-tail class distributions.
bias_and_limitations.generalizability_statement: Limited generalizability to clinical settings due to low resolution and aggregation from non-representative public sources.
bias_and_limitations.subgroup_coverage: No consistent subgroup coverage (e.g., age, sex, ethnicity) across sub-datasets.
bias_and_limitations.missing_data: Demographic and clinical metadata largely absent or inconsistent.

tasks_and_use.excluded_tasks: Detection, segmentation, report generation, or any task requiring spatial fidelity or high-resolution input.

data_origin.selection_rationale: Aggregated from existing public medical image datasets to enable standardized, lightweight benchmarking.
data_origin.aggregation_multisource: Aggregates ~708K 2D images and ~10K 3D images from multiple existing public sources.

population.target_population: Patients and subjects represented in underlying source datasets (e.g., dermatology, radiology, ophthalmology, pathology cohorts).

attribute_recording.unknown_proportion: Demographic attributes (age, sex, ethnicity) are not reported or standardized across sub-datasets.

annotation.annotation_method: Labels inherited from original source datasets; no unified annotation protocol applied during aggregation.
annotation.labeling_provenance: Labels derived from upstream public datasets; quality and consistency vary by sub-dataset.
annotation.label_noise_description: Label quality inherited from upstream sources; class balance and noise characteristics vary per sub-dataset.
